evals.name: fanout-sqs-sns-eventbridge
evals.prompt: We run a small order system on AWS: API Gateway, 3 Lambdas, DynamoDB, about 5,000 orders a day, a team of 4. When an order is created we notify billing and an email service, and next quarter there may be a third consumer (analytics). Should we use SQS, SNS, or EventBridge for the fan-out? I want your recommendation, not a design document. Write it to recommendation.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill forces one committed recommendation (no 'it depends'), an effort bucket, a numbered action plan, and escalation triggers for an architecture decision. A competent answer without it often lists all three options evenly or writes a mini design doc.
expectations: Gives an effort estimate using a Quick/Short/Medium/Large bucket

Commits to one primary fan-out option that fits 5,000 orders/day, a team of 4, and a likely third consumer: Names one option (SNS to per-consumer SQS queues, or EventBridge with one rule per consumer) as the answer and ties it to the stated scale, team size and third consumer

Rejected alternatives are named with concrete reasons: Each of the two rejected options gets a specific reason (e.g. plain SQS makes the producer write to every queue; EventBridge vs SNS trade-off on filtering, schema, cost or latency)
Follows the advisor response structure for an architecture decision: Has a 2-3 sentence bottom line, a numbered action plan, an effort bucket, and escalation triggers or 'when to reconsider'

Watch-outs are specific to the chosen fan-out: Names at least two concrete risks with a mitigation, e.g. at-least-once delivery needs idempotent consumers, a DLQ per consumer queue, alarms on queue age
Stays a recommendation, proportionate to the question: Fits on roughly one page, states any assumptions, no invented requirements or SLAs

scripted_checks.text: Gives an effort estimate using a Quick/Short/Medium/Large bucket

evals.name: rest-to-graphql-budget-freeze
evals.prompt: My team lead wants to migrate our internal admin tool from REST to GraphQL. It has 7 REST endpoints, one React frontend, and 3 developers. We cannot add any new AWS managed services this quarter because of a budget freeze. Give me a recommendation I can paste into Slack, written to answer.md. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, state it, and finish the work.
evals.expected_output: The skill biases toward the least complex option, forbids recommendations that contradict stated constraints (a CRITICAL gate item), and asks for escalation triggers. Without it, answers tend to present a balanced GraphQL pros/cons list or suggest AppSync despite the freeze.
expectations: Gives a clear, constraint-respecting answer: Recommends not migrating now (or a clearly bounded alternative) and does not propose AppSync or any other new managed service as the path forward

Reasoning fits 7 endpoints, one client, 3 developers: Explains why GraphQL's benefits (many clients, interconnected data, over-fetching) do not apply here and names its real costs (resolvers, caching, auth, N+1, learning curve)

Advisor structure: bottom line, action plan, effort, and triggers to revisit: Has a short bottom line, numbered next steps (e.g. list the team lead's pain points, try a BFF or endpoint tweak), an effort bucket or N/A with reason, and concrete conditions to revisit GraphQL
Short enough to paste into Slack and respectful of the team lead: Reads as a Slack message (a few short paragraphs or bullets), no condescension, no full design doc
